chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The best of your women is she who, when she is alone with her husband, removes for him the shield of modesty, and when she dresses up, she dresses up with it the shield of modesty.

key_terms.الْحَيَاءُ: hayā' — modesty, shyness, a virtue of high importance in Islamic ethics encompassing both inner character and outward decorum
key_terms.خَلَتْ: to be alone, to seclude oneself — used here for the private marital space
key_terms.دِرْعَ الْحَيَاءِ: the shield of modesty — a poetic metaphor describing modesty (hayā') as protective armor worn in public, which the wife sets aside in the privacy of the marital relationship

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about the best wife in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) describes the ideal wife as one who strikes a balance between intimacy and modesty — being uninhibited in private with her husband while preserving a dignified public presence. This teaching was directed to the early Shia community in Medina and Kufa, where questions of marital ethics and the boundaries of hayā' (modesty) were a subject of ongoing guidance from the Imams. The metaphor of 'dir' al-hayā'' (the shield of modesty) would have resonated deeply with an audience familiar with battlefield imagery, conveying that modesty is a protective quality to be worn appropriately, not a barrier between spouses.
